sentences.text: The type specimen of Wulagasaurus is a partial dentary, which is the tooth-bearing bone of the lower jaw.
Gregory S. Paul estimated Wulagasaurus to be 9 meters long and weigh 3 tonnes in 2010.

Wulagasaurus is a genus of saurolophine hadrosaurid dinosaur named after its discovery locality in Heilongjiang, China. Pascal Godefroit and colleagues named the genus Wulagasaurus in 2008. The only known species, W. dongi, was named in honor of the Chinese paleontologist Dong Zhiming.
Only partial remains of Wulagasaurus are currently known.
As a hadrosaurid, Wulagasaurus was an herbivore.
As a hadrosaurid, Wulagasaurus was an herbivore that walked by alternating between bipedal and quadrupedal positions.
Wulagasaurus is classified within the family Hadrosauridae and belongs to the subfamily Saurolophinae.

Remains of Wulagasaurus were found in a bonebed dominated by the lambeosaurine hadrosaurid Sahaliyania in the Yuliangze Formation of Heilongjiang, China. Wulagasaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
Researchers suggest Wulagasaurus was the most basal known saurolophine, providing evidence that saurolophines and hadrosaurids likely originated in Asia.
